chunks: I said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'We have unripened dates (raTba) and rice — what is obligatory upon us regarding them?'
He said (peace be upon him): 'As for the unripened dates (raTba), there is nothing upon you regarding it.'

And as for the rice — whatever was irrigated by the sky (rain), then with the one-tenth (tithe, 10%); and whatever was irrigated by the bucket, then half of the one-tenth (5%), from everything that you measure by the sa'a', or he said: 'weighed by the measure.'

key_terms.الأرز: Rice — a grain crop subject to zakat
key_terms.الدلو: Dalw — bucket; refers to manual irrigation methods
key_terms.الرطبة: Rațba — unripened dates or alfalfa/clover; a crop type exempt from zakat in this ruling
key_terms.الصاع: Sa'a — a traditional Islamic unit of dry measure (approximately 3-4 litres)
key_terms.العشر: 'Ushr — one-tenth (10%) tithe, the zakat rate for rain-irrigated crops
key_terms.نصف العشر: Nisf al-'ushr — half of the tithe (5%), the zakat rate for manually-irrigated crops

ai.seo_question: What is the zakat rate on rice and unripened dates according to Imam al-Kadhim?
ai.summary: Imam al-Kadhim (peace be upon him) provides a legal ruling on zakat obligations for two agricultural products: unripened dates (raTba) — which bear no zakat — and rice, which is subject to zakat at different rates depending on the irrigation method: one-tenth ('ushr, 10%) for rain-irrigated crops and one-twentieth (nisf al-'ushr, 5%) for manually-irrigated crops. This ruling reflects the classical Islamic principle that zakat rates are tied to the effort expended in cultivation. The narrator Muhammad ibn Isma'il was consulting the Imam about the specific produce he owned, receiving a direct and authoritative jurisprudential response.
